name: Neocaridina shrimp (red)
notes: The four colour groups share one tank and interbreed freely, so the lines will trend toward wild brown over successive generations. Separating a line needs a second tank, not a divider.

name: Neocaridina shrimp (yellow)
notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

name: Neocaridina shrimp (red and white)
notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

name: Neocaridina shrimp (orange and white)
notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

name: Fancy guppy
notes: Sex ratio unknown. If mixed, fry within weeks and a compounding bioload. Guppies take shrimplets, so recruitment in a shared tank depends on cover.

name: Albino mystery snail
notes: Adults are commonly given 2.5-5 gal each, so this group is the largest single bioload in the tank. Shell condition is the health signal to watch.

name: Red Racer nerite
notes: Grazes biofilm only and cannot breed in fresh water, so this group only ever shrinks. Losses are not replaced from within.

name: Otocinclus
notes: Species confirmed. Alone, and Otocinclus are shoaling animals - see the shoal minimum in `aqua species otocinclus`. The belly check is the health signal: rounded means feeding, flat or sunken is the warning.
